Practice first on a plate with foam — the pattern needs steady hand. For better visibility, use Angostura (deep colour). The bitters not only decorate — aroma releases with each sip alongside the foam.
Difford's Guide — Drop Art. Punch Drinks. Instagram bartending culture. Death & Co.
Aerated foams are a modernist cocktail technique (Dave Arnold, Tony Conigliaro 2010s): a small amount of aromatic liquid (tea, fruit syrup, spirit) is loaded into an N₂O siphon to create stable foams that float on the cocktail. Latest generation of classic egg/aquafaba foam.

Charge the siphon with 100 ml of base liquid + 0.5 g of stabilising protein (egg white or soy lecithin) + 1 N₂O cartridge. Shake, refrigerate 30 minutes. Apply a 1 cm layer on the freshly served cocktail. Foam lasts 20-30 minutes before collapsing.
Citrus foam on Aperol Spritz. Matcha tea foam on Espresso Martini. Cucumber-mint foam on Pimm's. Smoked foam on Old Fashioned. Yogurt foam on Lassi cocktail.
Practice with the siphon first — the mix can explode if not loaded properly. Protein-liquid ratio is critical: too little = foam dies; too much = rubbery texture. Serve immediately for best texture.
Arnold, Liquid Intelligence. Tony Conigliaro — 69 Colebrook Row. The Aviary Cocktail Book.
wiki.art.regions.italy-aperitivo-culture: The Italian aperitivo (19th century, Turin) is a pre-dinner social ritual with bitter cocktails (Negroni, Spritz, Americano) accompanied by free snacks. Today Milan and Venice are its capitals.
Vermouth from Turin (Carpano, Cinzano, Martini), Aperol and Campari from Padua and Milan, Veneto prosecco. The Piedmont-Veneto terroir is the cradle of modern bitterness.
Negroni, Aperol Spritz, Americano, Negroni Sbagliato, Garibaldi, Bicicletta, Hugo. Bites: olive ascolane, grissini with bresaola, focaccia.
Canonical hour: 18:00-20:00. Always order at a table with free cicchetti. In Venice the local Spritz uses prosecco, not champagne.
Regan, The Negroni (2015). Difford's Guide. Punch — Aperitivo Hour.
wiki.art.regions.italy-amaro-culture.des: Italian amaros are bitter liqueurs based on herbs, roots, barks and citrus, originating in medieval monasteries. Each region has its own: Averna (Sicily), Montenegro (Bologna), Fernet-Branca (Milan), Cynar (Padua), Ramazzotti.
wiki.art.regions.italy-amaro-culture.ter: Alpine herbs (génépi), Mediterranean (rue, hyssop) and southern citrus underpin the palette. Each distillery guards secret recipes with 25-40 botanicals.
wiki.art.regions.italy-amaro-culture.sig: Fernet-Branca neat as digestif. Amaro Averna on the rocks. Cynar Negroni. Montenegro espresso pairing. Black Manhattan with Averna.
wiki.art.regions.italy-amaro-culture.tip: Each amaro has its role: bittersweet aperitif (Aperol, Campari), herbal digestif (Fernet, Cynar), sweet after-dinner (Montenegro, Nonino).
wiki.art.regions.italy-amaro-culture.sou: Brad Thomas Parsons, Amaro (2016). Wondrich. Difford's Guide — Amaro section.
wiki.art.regions.italy-vermouth-piedmont: Piedmont (northern Italy) is the cradle of modern vermouth. Antonio Benedetto Carpano invented commercial vermouth rosso in Turin in 1786. Today Carpano (Antica Formula), Cinzano, Martini & Rossi and Cocchi are still active.
Trebbiano and Moscato Piedmont grapes as base. The alpine region brings wormwood (Artemisia absinthium), génépi, gentian root and other key Italian vermouth botanicals.
Carpano Antica Formula (world reference). Cocchi Vermouth di Torino. Cinzano Rosso. Classic Martini Rosso. Cocchi Storico di Torino DOP.
Vermouth rosso at cellar temperature (14°C) in wine glass. Canonical Negroni and Manhattan use it. After opening, refrigerate 1-2 months.
Carpano Distillery archive. Wondrich, Imbibe!. Difford's Guide — Vermouth.
wiki.art.regions.france-aperitif-traditi: France popularised the elegant aperitif (19th century): Lillet (Bordeaux), Suze (Auvergne), Dubonnet (Paris), pastis (Marseille), kir (Burgundy). Less bitter and more floral/herbal than the Italian aperitivo.
Cassis from Dijon (Burgundy), gentian from Massif Central (Suze), Provençal botanicals (pastis), Bordeaux grapes (Lillet). Terroir varies dramatically by region.
Kir (cassis + white) and Kir Royal. Lillet with tonic and lemon. Suze tonic. Pastis with cold water. Dubonnet on the rocks. Noilly Prat vermouth in Martini.
Kir is the most social aperitif of France. Pastis dilutes 1:5 (1 pastis: 5 cold water) to turn white. Lillet also serves in classic cocktails (Vesper).
Lillet archive. Pastis 51 — Marseille tradition. Wondrich, Imbibe!. Difford's Guide.
wiki.art.regions.france-cocktail-history: France embraced the American cocktail in the 19th century via Paris (Ritz American Bar, Hemingway at Harry's New York Bar). After US Prohibition, exiled American bartenders brought techniques to Europe: Frank Meier, Harry MacElhone.
Paris as absolute capital. Cognac and armagnac from the southwest, Champagne from Reims and Turin-imported vermouth. Champagne acidity defines French cocktails (French 75).
French 75 (Harry's Bar, Paris, 1915). Bloody Mary (Harry's, 1921). Sidecar (Paris, 1922). Mimosa (Ritz, 1925). Boulevardier (Harry's, 1927). White Lady (Paris, 1929).
Visit Harry's New York Bar (Rue Daunou, 5) and Ritz American Bar — temples of Parisian cocktail. Sidecar and White Lady are the most representative of the French style.
Wondrich, Imbibe!. Harry MacElhone — Harry's ABC of Cocktails (1923). Difford's Guide — French cocktail history.
wiki.art.regions.japan-bar-precision.des: Japan developed between 1960-2000 a unique cocktail school: geometric precision, slow rhythm, hand-carved ice, hard shake (Kazuo Uyeda's technique at Tender Bar). It is a technical school, not performative art.
wiki.art.regions.japan-bar-precision.ter: Tokyo (Ginza) as absolute epicentre. Bars Tender Bar, Bar High Five, Bar Star, Bar Trench. Japanese whisky (Yamazaki, Hibiki) as most-used base. Perfectly ripened citrus from eastern Japan.
wiki.art.regions.japan-bar-precision.sig: Hard Shake Daiquiri. Japanese Sake Highball. Toki Highball with carved sphere. Yuzu Sour. Bartender in tuxedo, minimal communication, impeccable presentation.
wiki.art.regions.japan-bar-precision.tip: In a Japanese bar, don't request modifications — trust the bartender. Consultation is discreet, almost silent. Reservation essential. Tipping is not accepted — service is on the bill.
wiki.art.regions.japan-bar-precision.sou: Kazuo Uyeda — Cocktail Technique (Tender Bar). Ueno Hidetsugu — High Five Tokyo. Bourdain, Parts Unknown — Tokyo. Difford's Guide.
The Japanese highball (whisky + soda 1:4) has been a national drink since 1956 when Suntory launched mass campaigns to democratise domestic whisky. Today izakaya chains serve millions per night.
Suntory whisky (Toki, Hibiki, Yamazaki) plus hyper-carbonated soda and clear ice. Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto are the capitals. Izakayas are the social stage.
Toki Highball (entry-level, ubiquitous). Hibiki Harmony Highball (premium izakaya). Yamazaki 12 Highball (high-end). Mizuwari (whisky with ice and water, more diluted than highball).
At izakaya: highball is a long-table drink, not a counter drink. Pair with yakitori, edamame, gyoza. Always ask 'tonic-free' — tonic masks the whisky.
Suntory corporate archive. Ueno Hidetsugu — High Five Tokyo. Imbibe Magazine — Highball revolution.
wiki.art.regions.mexico-cantinas.descrip: The Mexican cantina (19th century) is a popular tavern serving tequila, mezcal and pulque with free botanas (tapas). Historically prohibited to women and children. Today cultural heritage protected in CDMX and Guadalajara.
wiki.art.regions.mexico-cantinas.terroir: Historic centres of CDMX, Guadalajara (Jalisco) and Oaxaca are the epicentres. Tequila from Jalisco, mezcal from Oaxaca, pulque from Hidalgo. Botanas: basket tacos, sopes, panela cheese.
wiki.art.regions.mexico-cantinas.signatu: Tequila reposado with salt and lime. Charanda. Natural pulque (uncured). Margarita in traditional cantinero version. Sangrita with tequila. Modern Don Carajillo.
wiki.art.regions.mexico-cantinas.tips: Cantina La Ópera (CDMX since 1876), La Imperial (CDMX), Bar La Capilla in Tequila (where Don Javier invented the Batanga). Order from the botanas menu — free with each drink.
wiki.art.regions.mexico-cantinas.sources: Diana Kennedy, The Cuisines of Mexico. Eater Mexico City. INAH cantinas archives.
wiki.art.regions.mexico-pulqueria-tradit: The pulquería is a Mexican tavern specialising in pulque (pre-Hispanic fermented maguey aguamiel). Heyday in CDMX between 1880-1940 with thousands of locales; today cultural revival in Hidalgo and Tlaxcala.
Hidalgo and Tlaxcala (central highlands) are the production heart. 8-12-year-old pulque magueys. CDMX (historic centre, Coyoacán) has the most-visited revival pulquerías.
Natural pulque (white, sourdough flavour). Fruit-cured (pulque + blended fruit: strawberry, mango, pineapple, celery). Atole with pulque. Sangrita with pulque.
La Pirata, La Risa, Las Duelistas are classic CDMX pulquerías. Fresh pulque lasts only 24-48 hours — commercial isn't the same. 4-7% alcohol fermented drink.
Cuauhtémoc Camarena, El Pulque y Sus Mitos. Diana Kennedy. Eater Mexico City. INAH research.
wiki.art.regions.cuba-mojito-history.des: The Mojito has Cuban 19th-century origins — descended from 'El Drague' (1586) of Francis Drake (aguardiente + sugar cane + lime + mint). In 1942 Hemingway popularised it from La Bodeguita del Medio (Havana). Today the most-drunk cocktail in the world.
wiki.art.regions.cuba-mojito-history.ter: Havana is absolute epicentre. Cuban white rum (Havana Club 3), acidic Cuban lime, fresh yerbabuena (Mentha spicata), unrefined cane sugar. Local soda. All from Cuba.
wiki.art.regions.cuba-mojito-history.sig: Original Mojito (La Bodeguita del Medio). Strawberry Mojito (modern variant). Royal Mojito (with champagne). Hemingway Mojito (no sugar, more sour).
wiki.art.regions.cuba-mojito-history.tip: At La Bodeguita: 'Mi mojito en La Bodeguita, mi daiquiri en El Floridita' (Hemingway). Mint is slapped, NEVER muddled. Very cold soda. Quality white rum.
wiki.art.regions.cuba-mojito-history.sou: Bodeguita del Medio archive. Wondrich, Imbibe!. Curtis, And a Bottle of Rum. Difford's Guide — Mojito.
wiki.art.regions.cuba-bodeguita-floridit: Bodeguita del Medio and El Floridita

Two emblematic Havana bars linked to Ernest Hemingway. La Bodeguita del Medio (1942, Empedrado 207): birthplace of modern Mojito. El Floridita (1817, Obispo 557): birthplace of Constante Ribalaigua's frozen Daiquiri.
Habana Vieja. Bodeguita is a small bar with celebrity-signed walls; Floridita is elegant with Hemingway statue. Both serve Cuban rum, Cuban lime, local yerbabuena.
Bodeguita: classic Mojito, Cuba Libre. Floridita: Hemingway Daiquiri (no sugar, maraschino and grapefruit), frozen Daiquiri, Papa Doble.
Visit both on the same day following Hemingway tour. Bodeguita has run since 1942 unchanged. Floridita renovated interior in 2000 keeping bar and statue.
Bodeguita and Floridita archives. Hemingway letters. Wondrich, Imbibe!. Curtis, And a Bottle of Rum.
wiki.art.regions.peru-pisco-culture.desc: Pisco is Peru's national drink, DO grape spirit since 1991. Its historic cradle is the Ica region (south of Lima). Pisco Sour is the national cocktail, created in 1916 by Victor Vaughen Morris at Morris' Bar in Lima.
wiki.art.regions.peru-pisco-culture.terr: Ica, Lima, Arequipa, Moquegua and Tacna are the 5 DO producing regions. Pisco grapes: Quebranta (non-aromatic), Italia, Torontel, Albilla, Moscatel. No wood ageing.
wiki.art.regions.peru-pisco-culture.sign: Pisco Sour (Victor Vaughen Morris, 1916). Chilcano (pisco + ginger ale + lime). Capitán (pisco + vermouth). Pisco Punch (Duncan Nicol in SF). Algarrobina cocktail.
wiki.art.regions.peru-pisco-culture.tips: In Lima: Bar Maido, Central, Country Club's English Bar. Aromatic Pisco (Italia, Moscatel) for Royal Pisco Sour; Quebranta for Chilcano. No egg white = not a real Pisco Sour.
wiki.art.regions.peru-pisco-culture.sour: Bar Morris archive. Toro-Lira & Kasin, The Pisco Book (2010). Difford's Guide. Eater LA.
wiki.art.regions.brazil-caipirinha-cultu: The Caipirinha is Brazil's national cocktail, made with cachaça (fresh sugar-cane juice spirit), lime, sugar and ice. 19th-century rural origin in São Paulo. Today a Brazilian DO protected internationally.
All of Brazil produces cachaça (>30,000 brands) but Minas Gerais and Pernambuco lead. Artisanal vs industrial cachaça differ dramatically. Small acidic Brazilian lime is the star.
Caipirinha (canonical). Caipiroska (with vodka, modern variant). Batida de coco. Strawberry Caipirinha. Aged cachaça neat for sipping.
Whole lime with peel — peel oils are part of the flavour. Refined or demerara sugar. Good-quality white cachaça (Yaguara, Avuá Amburana). Muddle lime with sugar gently, don't destroy.
IBRAC archive. Curtis, And a Bottle of Rum. Difford's Guide. Holmberg, Cachaça.
wiki.art.regions.scotland-whisky-tour.de: Scotland has 5 DO whisky regions with their own personalities: Highlands (wide variety), Speyside (fruity elegant), Islay (peat and sea), Campbeltown (salty oily), Lowlands (soft herbal). Classic distillery tour starts from Edinburgh.
wiki.art.regions.scotland-whisky-tour.te: Speyside: 50+ distilleries (Glenfiddich, Glenlivet, Macallan). Islay: 9 distilleries (Lagavulin, Laphroaig, Ardbeg, Bowmore). Highlands: 30+ distilleries. Each region has specific microclimate and water.
wiki.art.regions.scotland-whisky-tour.si: Glenfiddich 12 (Speyside, global entry-level). Laphroaig 10 (canonical peaty Islay). Lagavulin 16 (mature Islay). Macallan 18 (premium Speyside). Springbank (unique Campbeltown).
wiki.art.regions.scotland-whisky-tour.ti: Classic tour: Speyside Whisky Trail (8 distilleries, 1 week). Intensive tour: Islay (3 days, 5 distilleries). Book visits in advance. Try whisky neat first, then with 5 drops of water.
wiki.art.regions.scotland-whisky-tour.so: Scotch Whisky Association. Broom, World Atlas of Whisky (2020). MacLean, Whiskypedia. SMWS publications.
wiki.art.regions.scotland-distillery-his: Distillation in Scotland has 600+ years. First written reference 1494 (Exchequer Roll, malt commissioned for Friar John Cor). 1823 law legalised commercial distilleries — before, most were clandestine. Victorian boom (1880-1900) consolidated modern brands.

River Spey (Speyside), peat water (Islay), local grains. Water quality determines character — Glenmorangie uses hard water from Tarlogie; Highland Park uses Mountain Pomicena water. Each distillery has its 'master water'.
Glenfiddich (1887, first with SMSW). Glenlivet (1824, first legal). Old Bushmills (Ireland, 1608 — world's oldest). Lagavulin (1816). Bowmore (1779).
Historic tour: Glenturret (1763), Strathisla (1786) — oldest active distilleries. Diageo Claive Museum (Edinburgh) covers 600 years of history. Essential visit for historic-whisky interest.
Scotch Whisky Association historic archive. MacLean, Whiskypedia. Broom, World Atlas of Whisky.
wiki.art.regions.ireland-pub-culture.des: The Irish pub is a social institution since the 16th century: drink + food + live music + community. Over 7,000 in Ireland. Guinness is the national beer since 1759 (Dublin); Irish whiskey (Jameson, Bushmills, Tullamore) is the national spirit.
wiki.art.regions.ireland-pub-culture.ter: Dublin (Temple Bar district), Galway (west), Cork (south), Belfast. Each region has its historic pub (The Brazen Head Dublin, 1198 — one of the world's oldest).
wiki.art.regions.ireland-pub-culture.sig: Guinness Draught in traditional pint (perfect pour: 119.5 seconds). Irish Coffee (1942, Foynes). Hot Whiskey (clove, honey, lemon). Black & Tan (Guinness + Bass).
wiki.art.regions.ireland-pub-culture.tip: At an authentic pub: live music (informal session of fiddle, banjo, tin whistle) usually starts 21:00. The Guinness pint is served in two steps (90-second settle between pours). Don't rush the sip.
wiki.art.regions.ireland-pub-culture.sou: Guinness Storehouse Dublin archive. The Brazen Head archive. Wondrich, Imbibe!. Difford's Guide — Irish Coffee.
wiki.art.regions.england-london-cocktail: London led the European cocktail renaissance from 1996 with Dick Bradsell at Match Bar. The revival gave way to a new generation: Tony Conigliaro (69 Colebrook Row, 2009), Ago Perrone (Connaught Bar), Ryan Chetiyawardana (Lyaness, Mr Lyan). Today London is the world capital of signature bartending.

Soho, Shoreditch and Mayfair are the cocktail neighbourhoods. Traditional British cocktails (Pimm's Cup, Vesper, Negroni) coexist with modernist creations and scientific techniques (clarification, fat-wash, sous-vide).
Bramble (Dick Bradsell, 1984). Espresso Martini (Bradsell, 1983). Cup of Tea (Conigliaro). Connaught Martini (Perrone). Mr Lyan signature sustainability cocktails.
Must-visit bars: Connaught Bar, American Bar at the Savoy, Dukes Bar, Scarfes (Rosewood), Swift, Tayer + Elementary. Book in advance. Casual smart dress code.
Dick Bradsell archive. Conigliaro, Drinks Lab. Difford's Guide — London bars. World's 50 Best Bars rankings.
wiki.art.regions.england-gin-craze.descr: Between 1720 and 1751 London experienced the 'Gin Craze': cheap domestic distillates, poor-quality gin flooded the city. 6,000 shops sold gin; widespread alcoholic poisoning deaths. William Hogarth painted 'Gin Lane' (1751) denouncing the chaos.
wiki.art.regions.england-gin-craze.terro: All London, especially East End (Whitechapel). Domestic gin was mixed with turpentine and sulphuric — real danger. The crisis led to the 1751 Gin Act regulating production.
wiki.art.regions.england-gin-craze.signa: Old Tom Gin (historic sweet style). Holland's Gin (genever, ancestor). Plymouth Gin (1793, cleaner style). London Dry (19th-century modern evolution).
wiki.art.regions.england-gin-craze.tips: Visit museums: Beefeater Distillery (London) has Gin Craze exhibit. Read 'Gin: The Manual' by Dave Broom for evolution. Compare Dutch genever vs London Dry to see the difference.
wiki.art.regions.england-gin-craze.sourc: Wondrich, Spirituous Journey. Broom, Gin: The Manual (2015). British Museum Gin Craze exhibit. Hogarth's Gin Lane (1751).
wiki.art.regions.usa-prohibition.descrip: Prohibition (Volstead Act, 1920) banned production, sale and import of alcohol in the US. 13 years of clandestine speakeasies, smuggling (rum-running from Caribbean, whisky from Canada), mafia (Al Capone, Lucky Luciano) and trials. Repealed by the 21st Amendment in 1933.
wiki.art.regions.usa-prohibition.terroir: NYC, Chicago, Detroit and New Orleans were the hubs. Speakeasies like '21' Club, The Stork Club, Manhattan operated clandestinely. Cocktails hid the bad taste of smuggled alcohol.
wiki.art.regions.usa-prohibition.signatu: Bee's Knees (lemon + honey + gin to mask bad alcohol). Sidecar (Paris, where many US bartenders fled). French 75. Mary Pickford (Cuba). Sweet cocktails dominated to mask industrial alcohol.
wiki.art.regions.usa-prohibition.tips: NYC tour: revival speakeasies (Please Don't Tell, Death & Co, Attaboy). Read Last Call by Daniel Okrent for detailed history. American bartenders emigrated to Cuba, Paris and London — exporting bartending.
wiki.art.regions.usa-prohibition.sources: Daniel Okrent, Last Call (2010). Wondrich. Difford's Guide — Prohibition era. PBS Prohibition documentary.
wiki.art.regions.usa-tiki-revival.descri: The tiki revival began in 2000 with Beachbum Berry recovering lost recipes from Don the Beachcomber and Trader Vic. Modern bars like Smuggler's Cove (San Francisco), Lost Lake (Chicago) and Sippin Safari (Atlanta) took the movement mainstream.
wiki.art.regions.usa-tiki-revival.terroi: California (Don the Beachcomber 1934, Trader Vic 1937) is the cradle. San Francisco is now the revival hub with Martin Cate's Smuggler's Cove. Hawaii as kitsch aesthetic inspiration.
wiki.art.regions.usa-tiki-revival.signat: 1944 Mai Tai (Trader Vic original recipe). Zombie. Jungle Bird (Kuala Lumpur 1973, reclaimed 2010s). Pina Colada (Puerto Rico, 1954). Painkiller (BVI).
wiki.art.regions.usa-tiki-revival.tips: To start: read Beachbum Berry's Sippin Safari (2007). Visit Smuggler's Cove (San Francisco), Lost Lake (Chicago), Strong Water (Anaheim). Tiki mugs are collectible art.
wiki.art.regions.usa-tiki-revival.source: Beachbum Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007). Cate, Smuggler's Cove (2016). Wondrich. Punch — Tiki revival.
wiki.art.regions.usa-craft-cocktail-revi: The American cocktail revival began in 1987 with Dale DeGroff at the Rainbow Room (NYC). Sasha Petraske opened Milk & Honey (NYC) in 1999 — pioneering modern speakeasy. The 2000-2010 generation (Audrey Saunders, Phil Ward, Eben Klemm) consolidated the school.
NYC is the epicentre. Milk & Honey, Pegu Club, Death & Co, Employees Only, Attaboy, PDT (Please Don't Tell), Dante. Pre-Prohibition classics recovered with premium ingredients and technique.
Modern Old Fashioned. Sazerac revival. Traditional Manhattan. Penicillin (Sam Ross, 2005). Paper Plane (Sam Ross, 2008). Trinidad Sour (Giuseppe González).
NYC tour: Death & Co, Attaboy, Dante, PDT (entry through Crif Dogs phone booth). Audrey Saunders is the 'godmother'. Read 'Regarding Cocktails' (Petraske) and the 'Death & Co' book.
DeGroff, The Craft of the Cocktail. Petraske, Regarding Cocktails. Death & Co (Ten Speed 2014). Punch — US revival.
wiki.art.regions.scandinavia-aquavit.des: Aquavit (akvavit) is the national spirit of Scandinavia (Sweden, Norway, Denmark), made from grains or potatoes with caraway and dill as main botanicals. Tradition since 15th century; consumed iced at smörgåsbord.
wiki.art.regions.scandinavia-aquavit.ter: Skåne (southern Sweden), Linie (Norway — aquavit travels in barrels by sea crossing the equator twice, attributing its profile). Denmark: Aalborg. Each country has its recipe.
wiki.art.regions.scandinavia-aquavit.sig: Aalborg Taffel Akvavit (Denmark). Linie Aquavit (Norway, equator-crossing). O.P. Anderson (Sweden). Iced in shot glass alongside smörgåsbord. Nordic Bloody Caesar with aquavit.
wiki.art.regions.scandinavia-aquavit.tip: Serve at -10°C in frozen crystal shot glasses. Drink in one shot after a salty bite (gravlax, herring). Skål before each shot — looking your companion in the eye.
wiki.art.regions.scandinavia-aquavit.sou: Linie Aquavit archive. Aalborg archive. Difford's Guide — Aquavit. Eric Asimov, NYT Aquavit articles.
wiki.art.regions.scandinavia-akvavit-rit: Scandinavian akvavit has codified social rituals: skål (eye-contact toast), snapsvisor (mandatory songs between shots) in Sweden, and the smörgåsbord as gastronomic context. At Christmas and Easter: julbord and påskbord with mandatory akvavit.
Stockholm, Copenhagen, Oslo — ritual capitals. Traditional smörgåsbord hall with long table, cold food, akvavit in central ice bucket.
Skål Brüderschaft (German/Swedish): toast with fixed gaze, drink, gaze again. Snapsvisor: short songs (5-10 seconds) ending in collective 'Skål!'. 12 different akvavits at a julbord.
Drink akvavit only after a salty bite — never on empty stomach. Initial skål always with the host. Don't skip snapsvisor — rude.
Anya von Bremzen, Mastering the Art of Soviet Cooking (parallel Nordic). Linie Aquavit. Eric Asimov NYT. Traditional Scandinavian cookbooks.
wiki.art.regions.korea-soju-culture.desc: Soju is the national spirit of South Korea, made from rice, sweet potato or tapioca. World's best-selling spirit (Jinro Soju leading). Deep social culture with strict service codes between generations.
wiki.art.regions.korea-soju-culture.terr: All South Korea. Jinro (Seoul), Chamisul, Andong (traditional soju). Modern soju has 16-25% ABV; traditional 35-45%. Process differs between industrial (charcoal-filtered) and artisanal (pot still distillation).
wiki.art.regions.korea-soju-culture.sign: Neat soju in Korean shot glass. Somaek (soju + beer, popular mix). Chamisul Fresh with yogurt. Soju cocktail with yuzu. Cojinganmi with fresh fruit.
wiki.art.regions.korea-soju-culture.tips: Etiquette: never pour your own soju — wait for elder or host to pour. Accept with both hands. Drink the first round in one shot. Pair with anju (Korean tapas: kimchi, samgyeopsal, banchan).
wiki.art.regions.korea-soju-culture.sour: Jinro Soju archive. Korean Drinks Culture Institute. Eater Seoul. Wondrich, Spirituous Journey.
Mekong is Thailand's national rye spirit, produced by Surapun since 1941. It's the base of popular Thai whisky alongside SangSom (better known in the West). Mix of fermented rice, molasses and herbal botanicals.
All Thailand. SangSom (best-selling) and Mekong (more traditional) lead. The northeast region (Isaan) produces traditional rural lao khao.
Mekong soda with lime. Mekong Mary (Thai Bloody Mary version). SangSom Bucket (ice bucket with SangSom + Coke + Red Bull, tourist phenomenon). Neat Mekong with spicy food.

In Thailand: Mekong + Coca-Cola + ice + lime is the universal combination. For an authentic experience, look for lao khao at rural markets. Carries 35% ABV — stronger than it tastes due to sweet flavour.
Surapun archive. SangSom archive. Eater Bangkok. Difford's Guide — Thai spirits.
wiki.art.regions.vietnam-rice-spirits.de: Vietnam has a millennial tradition of rice spirits (rượu). Rượu đế (common, clear, 30-40% ABV), Rượu cần (from bamboo tubes, ceremonial), Rượu nếp (from glutinous rice). Produced in every village with artisanal methods.
wiki.art.regions.vietnam-rice-spirits.te: Northern Hanoi (classic rượu đế), Hue (centre, traditional rượu cần), Mekong Delta (aromatic rice rượu). Each region has its variety.
wiki.art.regions.vietnam-rice-spirits.si: Rượu Đế (neat, in shot glass). Rượu cần (from communal pot with bamboo tubes, ceremonial ritual). Rượu nếp cẩm (with black fermented rice, slightly sweet). Modern cocktails with rượu (Hanoi bars).
wiki.art.regions.vietnam-rice-spirits.ti: In rural Vietnam: village rượu is safe if the family invites you; tourist street stuff can be dangerous. Pair with spicy food. The rượu cần ceremony requires 8-10 people around the pot.
wiki.art.regions.vietnam-rice-spirits.so: Vietnamese Beverage Culture Institute. Eater Vietnam. Difford's Guide — Asian spirits.
wiki.art.regions.india-feni-goa.descript: Feni is the traditional spirit of Goa (western India), recognised as GI in 2009. Two varieties: Cashew Feni (main, from cashew apple) and Coconut Feni (from coconut palm). Portuguese-Indian tradition since the 16th century.
wiki.art.regions.india-feni-goa.terroir: Goa: only producing region. Cashew apple ripens February-May. Each village has its small family distillery. Traditional double-distillation technique passed generations.
wiki.art.regions.india-feni-goa.signatur: Feni with fresh lemon and soda. Modern Cashew Feni cocktail. Urrak (first distillation, milder 15%). Garrafao (second distillation, 30-45% ABV). Indian Feni Bloody Mary.
wiki.art.regions.india-feni-goa.tips: In Goa: bars in Mapusa, Anjuna, Panjim serve authentic local feni. Exported commercial is industrial. Traditional feni has potent smell — locals describe it as 'aroma of Goa'. Warming drink for tropical climate.
wiki.art.regions.india-feni-goa.sources: Goa GI Feni archive. Eater India. Difford's Guide — Feni. The Hindu — Feni cultural articles.
wiki.art.regions.china-baijiu-banquet.de: Baijiu is China's national spirit, the world's most-consumed (5 billion litres/year). Produced in regional sub-styles: fenjiu, maotai (Guizhou), luzhou laojiao (Sichuan), qingxiang (Beijing). Central to the Chinese banquet with strict social codes.
wiki.art.regions.china-baijiu-banquet.te: Maotai (Guizhou): most expensive and prestigious. Luzhou Laojiao (Sichuan): best-selling. Fen (Shanxi): oldest (16th century). Each sub-style uses different grains and techniques (sorghum, qu — Chinese koji).
wiki.art.regions.china-baijiu-banquet.si: Moutai Feitian (Guizhou, China's official state wine). Luzhou Laojiao 1573. Wuliangye. Fenjiu. Mixed in modern cocktails (Beijing hipster bars).
wiki.art.regions.china-baijiu-banquet.ti: At banquet: gan bei ('bottom up', drink the whole shot) is protocol. Toast with the host, eye contact, glass down. Pair with fatty spicy food (yuxiang, mapo tofu). Start moderate — night is long.
wiki.art.regions.china-baijiu-banquet.so: Sandhaus, Drunk in China (2019). Maotai archive. Eater Beijing. Difford's Guide — Baijiu.
wiki.art.regions.ethiopia-tej-honey-wine: Tej is Ethiopian fermented honey wine, millennial, considered national drink. Made with honey + water + gesho (buckthorn leaf as bittering). Served in bercele (long-necked, rounded bottle). Tradition since the Axumite era (1st century).
All Ethiopia. Addis Ababa has tej beats (traditional venues). Honey comes from mountainous regions (Wolayta, Sidamo). Gesho gives the distinctive bittering character.
Traditional tej (5-15% ABV, sweet-bitter). Tej Berele at ceremonial festival. Modern honey wine cocktails (Addis Ababa bars). Tella (millet beer, complement).
In Ethiopia: visit an authentic tej beat in Addis. Drink straight from the shared berele. Pair with injera (sour flatbread) and wat (meat curry). Festival tej can reach 20% ABV.
Tej beats Addis Ababa archive. Eater Africa. Difford's Guide — Ethiopian beverages.
wiki.art.regions.mexico-mezcal-oaxaca.de: Oaxaca is the world capital of artisanal mezcal. 90% of world mezcal is produced there. The region combines agave diversity (espadín, tobalá, tepeztate, arroqueño, madre cuixe) with pre-Columbian techniques (earthen oven, tahona milling).
wiki.art.regions.mexico-mezcal-oaxaca.te: Sierra Norte and Valles Centrales of Oaxaca. Each town (Matatlán, Santiago Matatlán, Tlacolula) has family palenques. Altitude (1500-2500m), volcanic soil and local mezcal masters define the profile.
wiki.art.regions.mexico-mezcal-oaxaca.si: Young espadín (most versatile). Wild tobalá (floral). Tepeztate (vegetal). Arroqueño (intense smoky). Madre Cuixe (mineral). Pechuga (with chicken in distillation, ceremonial).
wiki.art.regions.mexico-mezcal-oaxaca.ti: Visit palenques in Santiago Matatlán (15 distilleries). Drink from clay jícara, never crystal caballito. Worm salt and orange slices are the accompaniment. Masters like Don Lorenzo, Don Aquilino are living legends.
wiki.art.regions.mexico-mezcal-oaxaca.so: Bowen, Mezcal: The History, Craft & Cocktails (Sterling 2020). CRM Mezcal regulatory. Eater LA — Oaxaca coverage. Schutes & Bank, Holy Smoke! (2020).
Tequila is Mexican DO of blue Weber agave, produced in Jalisco (epicentre) and parts of Nayarit, Guanajuato, Michoacán and Tamaulipas. CRT regulates since 1974. Three categories: blanco/silver, reposado (2-12 months wood), añejo (1-3 years).
Highlands (Los Altos) and Jalisco Valleys. Volcanic soil, 1500m altitude. Agave matures 6-8 years before harvest.
Blanco tequila for Margarita and Paloma. Reposado in Old Fashioned. Añejo neat. Don Julio 1942, Patrón Roca, Fortaleza, Tapatío.
Read the label: '100% agave' is essential. Mixtos contain added sugar. Visit distilleries in Tequila town and Arandas (Los Altos).
CRT Tequila archive. Bowen books. Difford's Guide.
wiki.art.regions.caribbean-rum-tour.desc: The Caribbean is the cradle of rum since the 17th century. Each island produces a style: Jamaica (funky, high ester), Cuba (smooth, coffee-tinged), Barbados (medium, round), Martinique (agricole from fresh juice), Venezuela (sweet aged).
wiki.art.regions.caribbean-rum-tour.terr: Jamaica: Hampden, Appleton, Worthy Park. Cuba: Havana Club. Barbados: Mount Gay (1703, oldest), Foursquare. Martinique: Clément, Neisson (AOC). Venezuela: Diplomático, Pampero.
wiki.art.regions.caribbean-rum-tour.sign: Daiquiri (Cuba). Mai Tai (Jamaica + Martinique rums). Painkiller (BVI, Pusser's). Ti' Punch (Martinique, agricole). Hurricane (New Orleans but Caribbean rums).
wiki.art.regions.caribbean-rum-tour.tips: Visit Mount Gay in Barbados (oldest, 1703). Hampden Estate Jamaica for funky rums. Habana Club Tour in Cuba. Distillerie Clément in Martinique.
wiki.art.regions.caribbean-rum-tour.sour: Curtis, And a Bottle of Rum. Cate, Smuggler's Cove. Difford's Guide — Rum.
wiki.art.regions.argentina-fernet-coke.d: Fernet-Branca with Coca-Cola is Argentina's informal national cocktail, especially in Córdoba. Argentina consumes 75% of world-produced Fernet-Branca. Deep social ritual among friends.
wiki.art.regions.argentina-fernet-coke.t: Córdoba as absolute capital. Buenos Aires, Rosario. Served in tall glass with lots of ice. Typical ratio: 1 part Fernet to 3 parts Coke.
wiki.art.regions.argentina-fernet-coke.s: Fernet con Coca (canonical). Fernandito (more diluted). Fernet on the rocks (more bitter, connoisseur). Branca Menta as variation.
wiki.art.regions.argentina-fernet-coke.t: In Córdoba: serve with lots of ice and Coke. Sip in social table. Fernet culture in Argentina is post-work, pre-dinner. Fernet-Branca is the only brand used — no substitutes.
wiki.art.regions.argentina-fernet-coke.s: Fernet-Branca Argentina archive. Eater Argentina. Punch Drinks — Fernet culture.
wiki.art.regions.hong-kong-bar-scene.des: Hong Kong is Asia's cocktail capital alongside Tokyo. Coalesces British influence (whisky, gin) with Chinese base (tea, techniques). Regular World's 50 Best Bars: The Old Man, Coa, Penicillin.
wiki.art.regions.hong-kong-bar-scene.ter: Central (financial district), Sheung Wan, Wan Chai are the cocktail neighbourhoods. Talent diversity (HK, Macao, Singapore, expat) defines the scene.
wiki.art.regions.hong-kong-bar-scene.sig: The Old Man (Hemingway-themed signatures). Coa (agave-focused, World #1 2021). Penicillin (sustainability-focused). Quinary (clarified cocktails).
wiki.art.regions.hong-kong-bar-scene.tip: Book in advance (essential). The Old Man and Coa need 3-4 weeks. Combine cocktail bar tour with traditional dim sum. Japanese whisky and mezcal are protagonists.
wiki.art.regions.hong-kong-bar-scene.sou: World's 50 Best Bars rankings. Eater Hong Kong. Punch.
wiki.art.regions.singapore-cocktail-scen: Singapore has a vibrant cocktail scene influenced by British colonial culture (Singapore Sling, 1915) and multi-ethnic diversity (Malay, Chinese, Indian, Peranakan cuisine). World #1 bars like Atlas and Native (#1 World 2022).
Raffles Hotel (Singapore Sling, Long Bar). Native (Asian botanicals only). Atlas (Marina Bay, art deco). 28 HongKong Street.
Singapore Sling (Raffles, 1915). Native cocktails with local ingredients (asam, gula melaka). Atlas Martini with Singaporean gin. Tippling Club tasting menus.
Original Singapore Sling at Raffles Hotel. Native and Atlas for modern innovation. Tippling Club for cocktail-food pairing. Always book.
Raffles Hotel archive. World's 50 Best. Eater Singapore. Difford's Guide — Singapore Sling.
wiki.art.regions.australia-bar-scene.des: Australia has a strong cocktail scene since 2010, led by Sydney and Melbourne. Australian Distilling Co (ADC), Four Pillars, Archie Rose Distilling lead local gin and whisky production. World #1 bars: Maybe Sammy, Black Pearl.
wiki.art.regions.australia-bar-scene.ter: Sydney (Maybe Sammy, Bulletin Place). Melbourne (Black Pearl, Bar Margaux). Australian bush botanicals (lemon myrtle, finger lime, anise myrtle) are signature ingredients.
wiki.art.regions.australia-bar-scene.sig: Cocktails with local gin (Four Pillars, Archie Rose). Native botanical Negronis. Pavlova cocktail. Sydney Spritz with Davidson Plum.
wiki.art.regions.australia-bar-scene.tip: Sydney: Maybe Sammy (Italian vibe), Bulletin Place (sustainability). Melbourne: Black Pearl (cozy speakeasy). Local product markets: Carriageworks Sydney, Queen Victoria Melbourne.
wiki.art.regions.australia-bar-scene.sou: World's 50 Best Bars. Eater Sydney/Melbourne. Australian Distilling Co. Difford's Guide.
wiki.art.regions.south-africa-brandy-his: South Africa produces brandy since 1672 when Jan van Riebeeck distilled the first Cape wines. Today one of the world's largest producers (KWV, Van Ryn's, Klipdrift). Internationally recognised pot still brandy.
Western Cape (Stellenbosch, Worcester, Robertson, Calitzdorp). Colombard and Chenin Blanc grapes for brandy. Karoo soil and Mediterranean climate define character.
KWV 10 Year Old (global entry-level). Van Ryn's 12 Year Old. Klipdrift Reserve. Brandy & Coke (informal national). Brandy Sour.
Visit Stellenbosch — SA brandy capital. KWV tour (Paarl) has magnificent cellar tour. SA pot still brandy is on par with premium cognac at lower price.
South African Brandy Foundation. KWV archive. Difford's Guide — Brandy.
wiki.art.regions.germany-beer-purity.des: The Reinheitsgebot (Purity Law, 1516) is the world's oldest food law still active. States that beer can only contain water, barley malt, hops and (later) yeast. Defines the character of German beer.
wiki.art.regions.germany-beer-purity.ter: Bavaria (cradle of Reinheitsgebot, Weisswurst, Oktoberfest), Rhineland (Kölsch, Altbier), Berlin (Berliner Weisse, Berliner Pils). Each region has its historic style.
wiki.art.regions.germany-beer-purity.sig: Bavarian Hefeweizen (Weihenstephan 1040). Münchner Helles. Pilsner (Bayern). Rauchbier (Bamberg, smoked). Berliner Weisse (sour-fruity). Kölsch (Cologne).
wiki.art.regions.germany-beer-purity.tip: Munich Oktoberfest (Sept-Oct) is the most iconic experience. Bamberg for Rauchbier and Schlenkerla. Berliner Weisse mit Schuss (with green or red syrup) is very refreshing in summer.
wiki.art.regions.germany-beer-purity.sou: Brewers Association of Germany. Reinheitsgebot historical archive. Mosher, Tasting Beer. Hieronymus, Brewing with Wheat.
wiki.art.regions.belgium-beer-monasterie: Belgium has 6 certified Trappist monasteries producing beer: Westmalle, Rochefort, Chimay, Orval, Westvleteren, Achel. Each makes 3-5 canonical styles. Tradition since 19th century, refined and codified.
Wallonia (Rochefort, Chimay) and Flanders (Westmalle, Westvleteren). Monastic subsoil water, proprietary yeasts, Belgian malt, imported hops. Lambic and gueuze additionally from Pajottenland.
Westvleteren 12 (world's best beer for years). Rochefort 10 Quadrupel. Chimay Grand Réserve. Orval (uniquely bitter-funky). Westmalle Tripel (origin of style).
Westvleteren: sold only at monastery (appointment). Chimay and Westmalle have tourist visits. Glass matters: each Trappist has its specific chalice. Drink at 12-14°C in contemplative sips.
International Trappist Association. Hieronymus, Brew Like a Monk. Belgian Beer Tourism.
wiki.art.regions.czech-pilsner-origin.de: Pilsen (Plzeň, Czech Republic) is the birthplace of Pilsner Urquell in 1842 — world's first clear golden lager. Created by Josef Groll using very soft local water and Saaz hops. Revolutionised beer globally.
wiki.art.regions.czech-pilsner-origin.te: Plzeň: very soft water (3°dH), Žatec (Saaz) hops from western Czech, Moravian barley malt, U-Hefe yeast (Bohemian lager). Natural sandstone caves for fermenting.
wiki.art.regions.czech-pilsner-origin.si: Pilsner Urquell (canonical). Budvar (Czech Budweiser). Staropramen Premium. Krušovice. Postal style: trinkbar — pint at cellar temperature (5°C), 3 cm foam.
wiki.art.regions.czech-pilsner-origin.ti: Visit Pilsner Urquell brewery in Plzeň — includes unpasteurised beer tasting from the barrel (tanková pivo). Historic breweries: U Fleku (Prague, since 1499).
wiki.art.regions.czech-pilsner-origin.so: Pilsner Urquell archive. Budweiser Budvar. Difford's Guide — Pilsner. Mosher, Tasting Beer.
Russia is the cradle of vodka — first written mention in 1430 (Chudov Monastery, Moscow). Dmitri Mendeleyev (periodic table creator) standardised 40% ABV in 1894. Deep social culture: zakuski, toasts, etiquette.
All Russia, but historic zones: Moscow, Saint Petersburg, Yaroslavl. Winter wheat (Moskovskaya), rye (Stolichnaya), potato (variants). Filtered spring water.
Stolichnaya (Stoli). Russian Standard Original. Beluga Gold Line. Beluga Noble. Mamont (Siberia). Served iced at -18°C.
Etiquette: iced vodka in shot glass, drink in one go. Pair with salty zakuski (pickles, herring, blini with caviar). Toast with fixed eye contact. Never drink without food.
Erickson, Vodka: A Global History (Reaktion 2014). Stolichnaya archive. Difford's Guide — Vodka.
Poland competes with Russia for vodka's cradle. First Polish document mentioning wódka in 1405. Polish rye vodka (Belvedere, Chopin) is international premium. Tradition of vodka with bisongrass (Żubrówka).
Bialystok (east, Żubrówka), Polmos (Lublin), Lewków (Belvedere). Polish rye, wheat (Wyborowa), potatoes (Chopin). Bison grass (Hierochloe odorata) in Żubrówka.
Żubrówka (with bisongrass, green-yellow colour, slightly herbal). Belvedere (premium rye, iconic bottle). Chopin (potato, single ingredient). Wyborowa Exquisite. Flavoured Soplica.
Żubrówka + apple juice is 'Szarlotka' (apple-pie cocktail). Visit vodka museums in Warsaw. Polish tradition distinguishes 'czysta' (clear) from 'gatunkowa' (flavoured) vodka.
Polish Vodka Association. Belvedere archive. Chopin archive. Difford's Guide.
wiki.art.regions.spain-sherry-jerez.desc: The Marco de Jerez (Cádiz, Andalusia) is Spanish DOP since 1933 — one of the world's oldest fortified wines. Unique solera and criadera system enables continuous dynamic aging. Five dry styles + two sweet.
wiki.art.regions.spain-sherry-jerez.terr: Sherry Triangle: Jerez de la Frontera, El Puerto de Santa María, Sanlúcar de Barrameda. Albariza soils (white limestone), Palomino grape (majority), Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel (sweet). Atlantic winds.
wiki.art.regions.spain-sherry-jerez.sign: Fino (Palomino, biological, light). Manzanilla (Sanlúcar, salty). Amontillado (transitional). Palo Cortado (rare, complex). Oloroso (oxidative). PX and Cream (sweet).
wiki.art.regions.spain-sherry-jerez.tips: Visit historic bodegas: Tio Pepe (González Byass), Lustau, Hidalgo La Gitana. Drink fino and manzanilla very cold (6-8°C). Tapas in Jerez/Sanlúcar inseparable. International Sherry Week every November.
wiki.art.regions.spain-sherry-jerez.sour: Liem & Barquín, Sherry, Manzanilla & Montilla (2012). Consejo Regulador Jerez. Sherry.wine. Difford's Guide — Sherry.
wiki.art.regions.portugal-port-douro.des: The Douro Valley (northern Portugal) is Port DOP since 1756 — world's first demarcated wine region. Sweet fortified wine from Touriga Nacional, Tinta Roriz, Touriga Franca grapes. Five styles: Ruby, Tawny, Vintage, LBV, White.
wiki.art.regions.portugal-port-douro.ter: Douro Valley (Cima Corgo, Baixo Corgo, Douro Superior). Unique schistose slates, sloped terraces, continental climate with extreme summer heat. 30,000 hectares of vineyard.
wiki.art.regions.portugal-port-douro.sig: Vintage Port (exceptional year, bottle aging). Tawny 10/20/30 years (barrel aging). LBV (Late Bottled Vintage). White Port (aperitif, with tonic). Ruby (young, fruit).
wiki.art.regions.portugal-port-douro.tip: Visit quintas in Douro: Quinta do Noval, Taylor's, Graham's, Niepoort. Vintage Port decants 24h before. Douro cruise is the best experience. Porto places: Vila Nova de Gaia (cellars).
wiki.art.regions.portugal-port-douro.sou: Mayson, Port and the Douro (Infinite Ideas 2018). IVDP archive. Wines of Portugal. Difford's Guide — Port.
wiki.art.regions.georgia-qvevri-wine.des: Georgia (Caucasian country) has 8,000 years of winemaking tradition — world's oldest. Qvevri method (buried clay vessels) declared UNESCO heritage in 2013. Origin of orange (skin-contact white) wines.
wiki.art.regions.georgia-qvevri-wine.ter: Kakheti (east, main region), Kartli, Imereti. Over 500 native grapes (Rkatsiteli, Saperavi, Kisi, Mtsvane). Alluvial soil and 200-700m altitude.
wiki.art.regions.georgia-qvevri-wine.sig: Qvevri orange wine (Rkatsiteli). Saperavi qvevri red. Modern Tsinandali white. Khvanchkara semi-sweet. Marani (traditional cellar with buried qvevris).
wiki.art.regions.georgia-qvevri-wine.tip: Visit Tbilisi and Kakheti region. Pheasant's Tears, Iago's Wine, Pheasant Hill — authentic qvevri producers. The supra (Georgian banquet) with tamada (toast master) is fundamental social ritual.
wiki.art.regions.georgia-qvevri-wine.sou: Woolf, Amber Revolution (2018). Georgian National Wine Agency. UNESCO Qvevri 2013. Difford's Guide.
wiki.art.regions.turkey-raki-meze.descri: Turkish rakı (similar to Greek ouzo, Italian sambuca — distinct but related) is Turkey's national anise spirit. Drunk during meze (Turkish tapas) with water and ice. Deep social culture around rakı sofrası.
wiki.art.regions.turkey-raki-meze.terroi: All Turkey. Tekirdağ and Edirne (Thrace) are main producing regions. Raisin, star anise, green anise seeds as base.
wiki.art.regions.turkey-raki-meze.signat: Yeni Rakı (classic, 45% ABV). Tekirdağ Rakısı (premium). Served in tall shot glass + water + ice: rakı turns milky (ouzo effect). Pairs meze: dolma, börek, kebab.
wiki.art.regions.turkey-raki-meze.tips: Etiquette: rakı + cool (not too cold) water + ice. Meze table lasts hours. Toast with 'Şerefe!'. Pair with sea fish (sea bass, sea bream). Don't mix with strong liquors in the same sitting.
wiki.art.regions.turkey-raki-meze.source: Yeni Rakı archive. Eater Istanbul. Difford's Guide — Rakı. Turkish Cultural Foundation.
wiki.art.regions.greece-ouzo-tradition.d: Ouzo is Greece's national anise spirit since 1856 (Tsillos in Tirnavos). Drinking it in mezedopolio (Greek meze tavern) is a Hellenic Mediterranean social ritual. Different from Turkish rakı by mix with flowers and spices.
wiki.art.regions.greece-ouzo-tradition.t: Lesbos (Plomari, ouzo capital), Tirnavos (mainland), Thessaloniki. Green anise, fennel, Chios mastic, coriander, cardamom. Aegean Sea defining the broth.
wiki.art.regions.greece-ouzo-tradition.s: Plomari Ouzo (Lesbos, premium). Tsillos (1856, first commercial ouzo). Mini Mytilene. Served cold with ice and water — turns milky (Ouzo effect). Mezes: tarama, tzatziki, kalamari.
wiki.art.regions.greece-ouzo-tradition.t: In Lesbos: visit Plomari distilleries. Drink ouzo at traditional seaside mezedopolio. Ratio: 1 ouzo + 1 water + 1 ice. Always pair with salty mezedes.
wiki.art.regions.greece-ouzo-tradition.s: Plomari Tsillos archive. Greek Spirits Federation. Eater Greece. Difford's Guide — Ouzo.
Arak is the traditional Levantine anise spirit (Lebanon, Syria, Palestine, Jordan). In Lebanon made from Obeideh grapes and anise. Central to Lebanese mezze in Beirut and Bekaa Valley.
Bekaa Valley (eastern Lebanon): Obeideh and Merwah vineyards. Historic distilleries: Touma, Massaya, Domaine des Tourelles (1868 — oldest active).
Touma Arak. Massaya Arak. Domaine des Tourelles Arak (1868). Served with ice + water: turns milky. Pairs tabbouleh, hummus, kibbeh nayye, falafel.
Bekaa Valley tours visit distilleries and wineries. Beirut: bars like Em Sherif, Couqley serve traditional mezze with arak. Compared to rakı/ouzo, arak is slightly less sweet and more herbal.
Domaine des Tourelles archive. Eater Beirut. Difford's Guide — Arak. Lebanon Wines Council.
wiki.art.regions.iran-history-of-wine.de: Iran (Persia) is the cradle of wine — archaeological evidence at Hajji Firuz Tepe dates to 5400 BCE (world's oldest). Continuous tradition until the 1979 Islamic Revolution banned alcohol. Today clandestine home production and exile.
wiki.art.regions.iran-history-of-wine.te: Shiraz (originally known for its wine; the Syrah grape may have roots here — though academic debate continues). Fars Province, Zagros Mountains. Historically unique terroir.
wiki.art.regions.iran-history-of-wine.si: Pre-revolution Shiraz wines (legendary). Today: Persian grape production in California (Diaspora) and home wine in Iran. Archaeological collections in museums.
wiki.art.regions.iran-history-of-wine.ti: Visit Iran National Museum (Tehran) to see prehistoric wine vessels. Shiraz grapes today are exclusively eating. Iranian diaspora produces wines in California (Khorshid Wines).
wiki.art.regions.iran-history-of-wine.so: McGovern, Uncorking the Past (2009). UCLA archaeological reports. Iran National Museum. Wine Folly.
wiki.art.regions.egypt-distillation-root: Ancient Egypt developed the first distillation techniques in the Alexandrian period (~3rd century BCE) — the alembic was invented by alchemist Maria the Jewess (Alexandria). Though not for alcohol initially, the techniques foundationed modern distillation.
Alexandria as ancient alchemic-scientific centre. Library of Alexandria preserved texts. Today archaeo-chemists study early distillers at Saqqara, Hierakonpolis.
Copper alembic (originally Egyptian-Alexandrian). Barley beer tradition (pyramid workers got 4-5L/day). Palm wine (imported from Lebanon and Galilee).
Visit Egyptian Museum (Cairo) for archaeological alembics. Modernised Library of Alexandria has alchemy exhibit. Read 'Alchemy' by Lawrence Principe to understand the influence.
Lawrence Principe, The Secrets of Alchemy. Egyptian Museum Cairo. McGovern, Ancient Wine. Wondrich, Spirituous Journey.
wiki.art.bartenders.jerry-thomas.title: Jerry Thomas
wiki.art.bartenders.jerry-thomas.descrip: Jeremiah P. 'Jerry' Thomas (1830-1885) is considered the father of modern American bartending. Worked at NYC's Metropolitan Hotel and other venues. Author of 'How to Mix Drinks' (1862), the first serious cocktail manual.
wiki.art.bartenders.jerry-thomas.career: Started as apprentice in New Haven aged 16. Toured the American West, Europe and Cuba absorbing techniques. Returned to NYC in 1851. Bar manager at the Metropolitan in the 1860s.
wiki.art.bartenders.jerry-thomas.signatu: Blue Blazer (flaming whisky tossed between two cups, his visual tour de force). Tom and Jerry (hot egg-yolk punch). Martinez (precursor to Martini). 10 fancy drinks codified in his book.
wiki.art.bartenders.jerry-thomas.tips: Read How to Mix Drinks (1862) reissue — foundation of all modern bartending. The Blue Blazer is dangerous performance, don't try at home.
wiki.art.bartenders.jerry-thomas.sources: Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862). Wondrich, Imbibe! (2007). NYC Historic Society.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-craddock.title: Harry Craddock
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-craddock.descr: Harry Craddock (1876-1963) was an American bartender who fled to London during Prohibition. Head of the Savoy Hotel's American Bar from 1920. Author of The Savoy Cocktail Book (1930), compiling 750 recipes — the most influential cocktail book of the 20th century.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-craddock.caree: Started in Cleveland (Ohio). Worked at Holland House (NYC) and Knickerbocker before Prohibition. Emigrated to London 1920. Head bartender at the Savoy from 1925. Co-founded UKBG (United Kingdom Bartenders Guild) in 1933.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-craddock.signa: White Lady (gin + Cointreau + lemon juice + egg white). Corpse Reviver #2 (gin + Lillet + Cointreau + lemon + absinthe). 750 recipes in The Savoy Cocktail Book.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-craddock.tips: The Savoy Cocktail Book 1930 edition is a collectible. Modern facsimile available. Origin of cocktails now considered pre-Prohibition classics.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-craddock.sourc: Craddock, The Savoy Cocktail Book (1930). Wondrich, Imbibe!. Difford's Guide.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-johnson.title: Harry Johnson
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-johnson.descri: Harry Johnson (1845-1933), Prussian-born bartender emigrated to the US, author of the Bartender's Manual (1882, expanded 1888 second edition). Contains one of the first documented descriptions of Manhattan, Martini and other seminal recipes.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-johnson.career: Born in Königsberg (Prussia, now Kaliningrad). Emigrated to SF 1862. Managed multiple bars and bartending schools in NYC and Boston. Considered the first 'professional bar manager'.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-johnson.signat: Manhattan (first documented version). Martini with orange bitters. Complete bar management tutorial (cleanliness, inventory, service).
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-johnson.tips: Bartender's Manual covers recipes and management — useful for anyone opening a bar. Available in modern reprint.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-johnson.source: Johnson, Bartender's Manual (1882, 1888). Wondrich, Imbibe!. Cocktail Codex.
wiki.art.bartenders.ada-coleman.title: Ada Coleman
wiki.art.bartenders.ada-coleman.descript: Ada 'Coley' Coleman (1875-1966) was the first female head bartender at the Savoy's American Bar (London, 1903-1925). Inventor of the Hanky Panky for actor Sir Charles Hawtrey. Pioneer of female bartending before the modern era.
wiki.art.bartenders.ada-coleman.career: Started at Claridge's Hotel. Moved to the Savoy in 1903. Head bartender until her retirement in 1925, succeeded by Harry Craddock. Served European royalty and Belle Époque celebrities.
wiki.art.bartenders.ada-coleman.signatur: Hanky Panky (gin + sweet vermouth + Fernet-Branca, c.1903). Signature Manhattan. Recognised as one of the most skilful bartenders of her time.
wiki.art.bartenders.ada-coleman.tips: The Hanky Panky is the bartender's bartender drink — try it if you love Negroni or Boulevardier. Today bartenders make their own riff with different amaros.
wiki.art.bartenders.ada-coleman.sources: Savoy archive. Wondrich, Imbibe!. Difford's Guide — Hanky Panky.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-mcelhone.title: Harry MacElhone
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-mcelhone.descr: Harry MacElhone (1890-1958), Scottish-American bartender, founder of Harry's New York Bar in Paris (1923). Creator of many canonical cocktails: Sidecar, Boulevardier, White Lady, Bloody Mary attribution.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-mcelhone.caree: Worked at Plaza Hotel NYC and Ciro's London before Paris. Bought the bar in 1923 keeping the original name. The bar attracted Hemingway, Fitzgerald, Bogart and American celebrities in Paris 1920-1950s.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-mcelhone.signa: Sidecar (1922, attributed). Boulevardier (1927). White Lady (1929). Bloody Mary (attributed to his employee Fernand Petiot, 1921). Harry's ABC of Cocktails (1923) book.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-mcelhone.tips: Visit Harry's New York Bar (Rue Daunou 5) — operating since 1911. Atmosphere and bar are unchanged. Order his original Boulevardier.
wiki.art.bartenders.harry-mcelhone.sourc: MacElhone, Harry's ABC of Cocktails (1923). Wondrich, Imbibe!. Harry's Bar archive.
wiki.art.bartenders.frank-meier.title: Frank Meier
wiki.art.bartenders.frank-meier.descript: Frank Meier (1884-1947), Viennese bartender at the Ritz Paris Bar from 1921-1947. Famous for his precision, discretion and secrecy (he was an Allied spy during WWII). Author of The Artistry of Mixing Drinks (1934).
wiki.art.bartenders.frank-meier.career: Started in Vienna, then London and NYC. Reached the Ritz Paris in 1921, manager until 1947. During Nazi occupation, passed information to the Resistance from his bar. Died of cancer in 1947.
wiki.art.bartenders.frank-meier.signatur: Bee's Knees (1930s, attributed). Brandy Daisy. Crusta. Hundreds of original recipes in The Artistry of Mixing Drinks. The Ritz Paris style (refined, sober).
wiki.art.bartenders.frank-meier.tips: The Artistry of Mixing Drinks (1934) available in reprint. His Bee's Knees is a classic — gin + honey + lemon. The Frank Meier spy story is a novel in itself.
wiki.art.bartenders.frank-meier.sources: Meier, The Artistry of Mixing Drinks (1934). Ritz Paris archive. Difford's Guide. Wartime espionage histories.
wiki.art.bartenders.charles-h-baker.desc: Charles H. Baker Jr. (1895-1987), American writer, traveller and bon vivant. Author of The Gentleman's Companion (1939, 2 vols.) and Jigger, Beaker and Glass (1939) — legendary drinking chronicles around the world in the 1920s-40s.
wiki.art.bartenders.charles-h-baker.care: Heir of textile fortune, travelled the world almost continuously 1925-1939 hunting exotic cocktails. Documented bars in Singapore, Havana, Macao, Paris, Manila. His books are chronicle + recipes.
wiki.art.bartenders.charles-h-baker.sign: Macao Cocktail. The Around-the-World Cocktail. Jamaican Quaff. A hundred exotic drinks documented with anecdotes. Model of the 'cocktail traveler'.
wiki.art.bartenders.charles-h-baker.tips: His books available in modern reprint (Beaufort Books). Pioneer of lifestyle cocktail writing — between Hemingway and travel guide. Highly entertaining read.
wiki.art.bartenders.charles-h-baker.sour: Baker, The Gentleman's Companion (1939). Baker, Jigger, Beaker and Glass (1939). Wondrich. Punch.
wiki.art.bartenders.david-embury.title: David A. Embury
wiki.art.bartenders.david-embury.descrip: David A. Embury (1886-1960), New York lawyer and amateur bartender, author of The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks (1948) — one of the 20th century's most influential cocktail books. Codified cocktail theory (base + modifier + accent + citrus) still standard teaching.
wiki.art.bartenders.david-embury.career: Lawyer by profession, bartending was hobby. His self-published book (1948) became the bible of the post-Prohibition generation. 4 revised editions. Died 1960; book kept influencing until the 2000s revival.
wiki.art.bartenders.david-embury.signatu: '6:1:1' doctrine for dry Martini (6 parts gin to 1 vermouth). Sour theory (base : sweet : sour 8:3:2). Philosophy of simplicity: 'less is more' in cocktails.
wiki.art.bartenders.david-embury.tips: The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks (1948) — required reading. Embury was anti-decoration purist; opponent of excessive sugar. His 8:3:2 formula remains the Sour gold standard.
wiki.art.bartenders.david-embury.sources: Embury, The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks (1948). Wondrich. Cocktail Codex (Death & Co).
wiki.art.bartenders.trader-vic.title: Trader Vic (Victor Bergeron)
wiki.art.bartenders.trader-vic.descripti: Victor Jules Bergeron (1902-1984), co-creator with Don the Beachcomber of the tiki movement. Opened Trader Vic's in Oakland (1934, originally Hinky Dink's). Inventor of the original Mai Tai (1944). Built global tiki restaurant chain.
wiki.art.bartenders.trader-vic.career: Oakland bartender with no left leg (amputated for bone TB). Visited Cuba, Hawaii, China for inspiration. Turned Hinky Dink's into Trader Vic's in 1937. Chain of 25+ restaurants in the 70s. Died 1984.
wiki.art.bartenders.trader-vic.signature: Original Mai Tai (1944, Jamaican rum + lime + orgeat + curaçao). Fog Cutter. Scorpion. Samoan Fog Cutter. Over 200 tiki cocktails in his books.
wiki.art.bartenders.trader-vic.tips: Visit Trader Vic's in Oakland (operating since 1934). His 'Bartender's Guide' (1947, 1972) has original recipes. The original Mai Tai is very different from commercial — try it.
wiki.art.bartenders.trader-vic.sources: Bergeron, Bartender's Guide (1947). Berry, Sippin' Safari. Cate, Smuggler's Cove. Trader Vic's archive.
Ernest Raymond Beaumont Gantt (1907-1989), original pioneer of tiki movement. Opened Don the Beachcomber in Hollywood (1934) — world's first tiki bar, predecessor to Trader Vic. Inventor of Zombie and many tiki classics.

Born in Texas, merchant sailor, toured Caribbean and South Pacific. Returned to Hollywood and opened Don the Beachcomber (1934). WW2 military service. After return, expanded chain. Conflict with ex-wife Sunny Sund led to complex franchise.
Zombie (1934, original 8-ingredient secret formula). Beach Comber. Pearl Diver. Cobra's Fang. Navy Grog. Original tiki aesthetic (Polynesian temples, torches, ceramic ware).
Berry resurrected the original Zombie in 'Beachbum Berry Remixed' (2009). Cocktail has 8 ingredients — done right, very different from commercial. Reserve time to build it.
Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007). Berry, Remixed (2009). Cate, Smuggler's Cove. Don the Beachcomber archive.
wiki.art.bartenders.vic-bergeron.title: Vic Bergeron (aka Trader Vic)
wiki.art.bartenders.vic-bergeron.descrip: Victor Jules Bergeron Jr. (1902-1984) — variant of the same Trader Vic. Full biographical data is in the Trader Vic article. This entry exists as historical redirect to the main article.
wiki.art.bartenders.vic-bergeron.career: See Trader Vic article. The difference is only nominal — some bartenders/historians refer to 'Vic Bergeron' as historical person and 'Trader Vic' as brand.
wiki.art.bartenders.vic-bergeron.signatu: Original Mai Tai 1944. See Trader Vic.
wiki.art.bartenders.vic-bergeron.tips: For full details, see the Trader Vic article. Bergeron and Trader Vic are the same person.
wiki.art.bartenders.vic-bergeron.sources: See Trader Vic. Bergeron, Bartender's Guide (1947).
Salvatore Calabrese (b. 1955), Italian-British bartender nicknamed 'The Maestro'. Head of London's Lanesborough Hotel for 30+ years. Guinness record for preparing the world's most expensive cocktail (Salvatore's Legacy, £5,500).
Born in Maiori (Amalfi Coast). Started in family hotel. Reached London 1981. Lanesborough Library Bar 1989-2007. Tiger Salvatore's Bar at Playboy Club. Author of 9 books.
Salvatore's Legacy (£5,500 cocktail with 1788 cognac). Breakfast Martini (1996). Spicy Fifty. Famous Cognac. Specialist in aged and vintage spirits.
His book 'Classic Cocktails' (1997) is one of the best fundamental manuals. Breakfast Martini (gin + marmalade + Cointreau + lemon) is viral in modern bars.
Calabrese, Classic Cocktails (1997). Difford's Guide. Salvatore's Bar archive. Guinness records.
wiki.art.bartenders.dale-degroff.title: Dale DeGroff
wiki.art.bartenders.dale-degroff.descrip: Dale DeGroff (b. 1948), 'King Cocktail', leader of the American cocktail revival. Head bartender at Rainbow Room (NYC, 1987-1999). Recovered forgotten pre-Prohibition cocktails and formed the 2000s generation (Saunders, Petraske, Ward).
wiki.art.bartenders.dale-degroff.career: Started at Hotel Bel-Air (LA). Back to NYC, Rainbow Room in 1987 invited by Joe Baum. Founded Beverage Alcohol Resource (BAR) in 2003 — first formal bartending education programme. Author 'The Craft of the Cocktail' (2002).
wiki.art.bartenders.dale-degroff.signatu: Rainbow Room signature cocktails (modern Whiskey Smash, etc.). Influence on entire post-2000 generation. The Craft of the Cocktail foundational book.
wiki.art.bartenders.dale-degroff.tips: Read The Craft of the Cocktail (2002) — fundamental modern manual. DeGroff is 'the godfather' of US revival. His pedagogical role is comparable to Jerry Thomas in his era.
wiki.art.bartenders.dale-degroff.sources: DeGroff, The Craft of the Cocktail (2002). BAR archive. Rainbow Room archive. Wondrich, Imbibe!.
wiki.art.bartenders.audrey-saunders.desc: Audrey Saunders, 'Libation Goddess', protégée of Dale DeGroff. Head bartender at Bemelmans Bar (Carlyle Hotel NYC) and founder of Pegu Club (NYC, 2005). Co-creator of the cocktail revival alongside DeGroff and Petraske.
wiki.art.bartenders.audrey-saunders.care: Started at Beverage Alcohol Resource with DeGroff. Bemelmans Bar (Carlyle). Pegu Club 2005-2020 — one of the most influential bars of the modern era. Mentored Phil Ward, Brian Miller, Eben Klemm.
wiki.art.bartenders.audrey-saunders.sign: Old Cuban (2003, rum + champagne + mint + lime). Tantris Sidecar. Earl Grey MarTEAni (2003, gin + Earl Grey + lemon + egg white). Elegant technical style, premium ingredient-based.
wiki.art.bartenders.audrey-saunders.tips: The Old Cuban is one of the best cocktails of the 21st century — copy the cucumber and lemonpeel of the original. Earl Grey MarTEAni was revolutionary for using tea as base.
wiki.art.bartenders.audrey-saunders.sour: Pegu Club archive. PUNCH — Audrey Saunders profiles. Difford's Guide — Old Cuban.
wiki.art.bartenders.sasha-petraske.title: Sasha Petraske
wiki.art.bartenders.sasha-petraske.descr: Sasha Petraske (1973-2015), foundational figure of the modern speakeasy. Founder of Milk & Honey (NYC, 1999), Little Branch (NYC, 2005), Dutch Kills (Queens), Attaboy (NYC). Died prematurely in 2015 aged 42. Son of Yiddish writer.
wiki.art.bartenders.sasha-petraske.caree: Self-taught bartender. Milk & Honey 1999 — first modern speakeasy (entry by phone reservation only). Strict rules: dress code, no shouting, no perfumes. Massively influenced 5 bartender generations.
wiki.art.bartenders.sasha-petraske.signa: Penicillin (Sam Ross, 2005, at Milk & Honey). Modern canonical Old Fashioned. Milk & Honey's five rules. Posthumous book 'Regarding Cocktails' (2016).
wiki.art.bartenders.sasha-petraske.tips: Read Regarding Cocktails (2016) compiled by Georgette Moger-Petraske (wife). The Five Rules: 1) no orders not phrased as questions, 2) no shouting, 3) gentlemen greet ladies, 4) no strong perfumes, 5) no lobby.
wiki.art.bartenders.sasha-petraske.sourc: Petraske (posthumous), Regarding Cocktails (2016). Milk & Honey archive. PUNCH — Petraske obituary.
wiki.art.bartenders.julie-reiner.title: Julie Reiner
wiki.art.bartenders.julie-reiner.descrip: Julie Reiner (b. 1971), pioneering bartender of the new American female generation. Co-founder of Flatiron Lounge (NYC, 2003) and Clover Club (Brooklyn, 2008). Specialist in modernised classic tropical cocktails. Author 'The Craft Cocktail Party' (2015).
wiki.art.bartenders.julie-reiner.career: Born in Honolulu (Hawaii). Started at Carrera Lounge (Honolulu). Reached NYC in 1997. Flatiron Lounge 2003 (seasonal cocktails). Clover Club 2008 (homage to Philadelphia 1882). Mentored Lynnette Marrero, Ivy Mix.
wiki.art.bartenders.julie-reiner.signatu: Modern Brown Derby. Flatiron tropical cocktails. Clover Club cocktail (bar signature). Style: seasonal cocktails, premium ingredients, elegant feminine aesthetic.
wiki.art.bartenders.julie-reiner.tips: Visit Clover Club in Brooklyn — one of NYC's best cocktail bars. 'Craft Cocktail Party' (2015) has accessible home recipes.
wiki.art.bartenders.julie-reiner.sources: Reiner, The Craft Cocktail Party (2015). Clover Club archive. PUNCH — Julie Reiner profile.
wiki.art.bartenders.dushan-zaric.title: Dushan Zaric
wiki.art.bartenders.dushan-zaric.descrip: Dushan Zaric (b. 1972), Serbian-American bartender, co-founder of Employees Only (NYC, 2004) — pioneer of the New York revival. Co-author 'You Didn't Hear It From Us' (2010) — manual of philosophy and technique of modern bartending.
wiki.art.bartenders.dushan-zaric.career: Born in Belgrade, reached NYC 1998. Worked at Pravda and others. Co-founded Employees Only (Greenwich Village) with 4 partners in 2004. Bar expanded to Singapore, Hong Kong, Sydney, Miami.
wiki.art.bartenders.dushan-zaric.signatu: Ginger Smash. Mata Hari (mezcal + Chambord + lime). Provençal Mary. Mentored Naren Young, several Employees Only generations.
wiki.art.bartenders.dushan-zaric.tips: Employees Only is a must-visit in NYC. His book (2010) covers both recipes and bar ethos. Hospitality is central — employees are treated as protagonists.
wiki.art.bartenders.dushan-zaric.sources: Zaric & Kosmas, You Didn't Hear It From Us (2010). Employees Only archive. PUNCH.
wiki.art.bartenders.jim-meehan.title: Jim Meehan
wiki.art.bartenders.jim-meehan.descripti: Jim Meehan (b. 1975), American bartender, founder of PDT (Please Don't Tell, NYC, 2007) — iconic speakeasy entered through a Crif Dogs phone booth. Author of PDT Cocktail Book (2011) — one of the bestselling cocktail books of the revival.
wiki.art.bartenders.jim-meehan.career: Started at Pegu Club's Big Bar with Audrey Saunders. PDT 2007 with Brian Shebairo. Author PDT Cocktail Book (2011), Meehan's Bartender Manual (2017). Educational director Tales of the Cocktail.
wiki.art.bartenders.jim-meehan.signature: Benton's Old Fashioned (Bacon-washed bourbon, 2007). PDT signature cocktails. Eastside (gin + cucumber + mint + lime). Style: premium ingredients + storytelling.
wiki.art.bartenders.jim-meehan.tips: PDT requires phone reservation. PDT Cocktail Book (2011) has 300+ recipes. Meehan's Bartender Manual (2017) is the most current technical manual of the generation.
wiki.art.bartenders.jim-meehan.sources: Meehan, PDT Cocktail Book (2011). Meehan's Bartender Manual (2017). PDT archive.
wiki.art.bartenders.ago-perrone.title: Ago Perrone
wiki.art.bartenders.ago-perrone.descript: Agostino 'Ago' Perrone (b. 1974), Italian bartender based in London. Director of Mixology at Connaught Bar (Mayfair) — World's #1 Bar (50 Best 2020, 2021). Pioneer of the Italian premium-elegant cocktail school.
wiki.art.bartenders.ago-perrone.career: Born in Calabria. Reached London 2000. Worked at Tini Caffè, Como Hotel, Light Bar before Connaught. Director of mixology at Connaught Bar since 2008. Built world-reference team.
wiki.art.bartenders.ago-perrone.signatur: Connaught Martini (made tableside with 7-bitters menu). Reine de Saba. Modernised Vesper. Style: Italian precision, tableside presentation, mise-en-scène.
wiki.art.bartenders.ago-perrone.tips: Connaught Bar requires reservation — Martini made tableside, 7-minute ritual. Bartenders in black tie. Hospitality is the heart. Drink Martini with bitter of your choice.
wiki.art.bartenders.ago-perrone.sources: Connaught Bar archive. World's 50 Best Bars. PUNCH — Perrone profiles.
wiki.art.bartenders.simone-caporale.desc: Simone Caporale (b. 1985), Italian bartender. Co-founder of Sips Barcelona (World's 50 Best Bars #1 2023). Previously at Artesian (London Langham). Pioneer of European 'second wave' bartending.
wiki.art.bartenders.simone-caporale.care: Italy, then London. Artesian at the Langham 2010-2015 — World's #1 four consecutive years. Co-founded Sips Barcelona in 2021 with Marc Álvarez. Sips won World's #1 in 2023.
wiki.art.bartenders.simone-caporale.sign: Liquid Pop (Sips signature). Glamour Martini. Style: modernist technique + showmanship + low-ABV cocktails. Pioneer of premium non-alcoholic base cocktails.
wiki.art.bartenders.simone-caporale.tips: Sips Barcelona in Eixample — reservation essential. Small bar (40 seats), 7-step cocktail tasting menu. Called 'next-gen bartending'.
wiki.art.bartenders.simone-caporale.sour: Sips Barcelona archive. World's 50 Best 2023. PUNCH — Caporale profile.
wiki.art.bartenders.alex-kratena.title: Alex Kratena
wiki.art.bartenders.alex-kratena.descrip: Alex Kratena (b. 1980), Czech bartender based in London. Artesian head bartender during World's #1 era (2012-2015). Co-founded Tayer + Elementary (London) in 2019. Specialist in sustainability and conceptual cocktail design.
wiki.art.bartenders.alex-kratena.career: Czech Republic. London ~2005. Artesian 2010-2015 — his tenure was when the bar won #1 four consecutive years. Tayer + Elementary 2019 — dual sustainable bar. Co-founder of Pioneer Spirits.
wiki.art.bartenders.alex-kratena.signatu: Tea Time at Artesian (themed signature menus). Mr Wolf (Tayer signature). Style: conceptual, narrative, sustainability-driven.
wiki.art.bartenders.alex-kratena.tips: Tayer + Elementary in Shoreditch (London) — two bars in one. Elementary is casual with cocktail tasting menu. Tayer is elegant with conceptual signatures.
wiki.art.bartenders.alex-kratena.sources: Artesian archive. Tayer + Elementary archive. World's 50 Best.
wiki.art.bartenders.tony-conigliaro.desc: Tony Conigliaro (b. 1971), Italian-British bartender, father of European 'modernist cocktail'. Founder of 69 Colebrook Row (London, 2009) and The Drinks Factory (R&D lab). Pioneer of aerated foams, rotovap, scientific techniques.
wiki.art.bartenders.tony-conigliaro.care: London 90s. Shochu Lounge at Roka 2004-2008. 69 Colebrook Row 2009 — his public lab. Drinks Factory: R&D lab with stills and rotovaps. Co-author 'Drinks' (2009) and 'The Cocktail Lab' (2013).
wiki.art.bartenders.tony-conigliaro.sign: Aerated Negroni. Cup of Tea cocktail (Earl Grey teabag served in cocktail). Whisky Sour redux. Style: laboratory cocktails, sustainability, slow-tempo elegance.
wiki.art.bartenders.tony-conigliaro.tips: 69 Colebrook Row is 'Tony's lab'. Recipes like Aerated Negroni require N₂O whipper. Read The Cocktail Lab (2013) to understand the scientific philosophy.
wiki.art.bartenders.tony-conigliaro.sour: Conigliaro, Drinks (2009). Conigliaro, The Cocktail Lab (2013). 69 Colebrook Row archive.
Ryan Chetiyawardana 'Mr Lyan' (b. 1985), British bartender, sustainability pioneer in bartending. Founder of Lyaness (London, World #5), Cub, Super Lyan (Amsterdam). Multiple Bartender of the Year (2015, 2017).
Started at White Lyan (London 2013), first 'no-perishables' bar (no lime, ice, fresh citrus). Evolved to Dandelyan (2014) and Lyaness (2019). Modern Cub with sustainability as core.
Bone Dry Martini. Strawberry-Skin Cocktail. Reusable Lemonade. Style: sustainability, scientific technique, infusions, conscious packaging.
Lyaness in Sea Containers Hotel (Southbank). Sustainability menu changes constantly. White Lyan closed but the book 'Good Together' (2020) documents the philosophy.
Chetiyawardana, Good Together (2020). Lyaness archive. World's 50 Best Bars.
wiki.art.bartenders.naren-young.title: Naren Young
wiki.art.bartenders.naren-young.descript: Naren Young (b. 1973), Australian-American bartender. Director of beverage at Dante NYC (World's #1 2019). Pioneer of Italian aperitivo in the US. Co-author 'Dante: The Cocktail Bible' (2022).
wiki.art.bartenders.naren-young.career: Born in Sydney. Worked at Saxon + Parole, Patent Pending NYC. Dante NYC since 2015 when the Linden Pride/Nathalie brothers took the historic restaurant (West Village, opened 1915).
wiki.art.bartenders.naren-young.signatur: Dante Garibaldi (with fresh emulsified orange juice). Garibaldi-style cocktails. Dante aperitivo programme. Style: Italian aperitivo modernised, all-day cafe-bar concept.
wiki.art.bartenders.naren-young.tips: Dante NYC on MacDougal Street — visit for Negroni or Garibaldi. Dante's Garibaldi uses specialised juicer to emulsify orange — unique texture.
wiki.art.bartenders.naren-young.sources: Young, Dante: The Cocktail Bible (2022). Dante NYC archive. World's 50 Best 2019.
wiki.art.bartenders.tess-posthumus.title: Tess Posthumus
wiki.art.bartenders.tess-posthumus.descr: Tess Posthumus (b. 1986), Dutch bartender, owner of Flying Dutchmen Cocktails (Amsterdam) and Dutch Courage (Amsterdam). Multiple international awards, Bartender of the Year Netherlands. Advocate of European female bartending.
wiki.art.bartenders.tess-posthumus.caree: Amsterdam since 2008. Worked at Door 74 (Amsterdam speakeasy pioneer). Founded Dutch Courage (Singel, 2013) and Flying Dutchmen Cocktails (Negen Straatjes, 2017). Active in European consulting and education.
wiki.art.bartenders.tess-posthumus.signa: Dutch Courage signature menu (genever-based cocktails). Flying Dutchmen Mai Tai. Style: revival of Dutch genever (jenever) in modern cocktails.
wiki.art.bartenders.tess-posthumus.tips: Dutch Courage in Amsterdam — focus on genever (historic Dutch gin). Flying Dutchmen is more experimental. Tess is the reference for genever-based cocktails.
wiki.art.bartenders.tess-posthumus.sourc: Dutch Courage archive. Flying Dutchmen Cocktails. PUNCH — European bartending.
wiki.art.bartenders.monica-berg.title: Monica Berg
wiki.art.bartenders.monica-berg.descript: Monica Berg (b. 1985), Norwegian-British bartender. Co-founder of Tayer + Elementary (London, 2019) with Alex Kratena. Co-founder of Pioneer Spirits and P(OUR) — platform discussing the future of bartending.
wiki.art.bartenders.monica-berg.career: Norway. Pollen Street Social, Aqua Shard before Tayer. Tayer + Elementary 2019. Pioneer Spirits (premium spirits line with sustainability). Activist for inclusion and sustainability in industry.
wiki.art.bartenders.monica-berg.signatur: Mr Wolf (Tayer signature). Conceptual cocktail tasting menus. Style: conceptual, narrative-driven, sustainability ethics.
wiki.art.bartenders.monica-berg.tips: Tayer in Shoreditch. Elementary (casual) is the daily bar; Tayer is elegant for cocktail tasting. Her public voice on industry ethics is a reference.
wiki.art.bartenders.monica-berg.sources: Tayer + Elementary archive. Pioneer Spirits. P(OUR) magazine.
wiki.art.bartenders.ivy-mix.title: Ivy Mix
wiki.art.bartenders.ivy-mix.description: Ivy Mix (b. 1983), American bartender, co-founder of Leyenda (Brooklyn, 2015) — bar focused on agave and Latin spirits. Speed Rack co-creator (international female competition, 2011). Author 'Spirits of Latin America' (2020).
wiki.art.bartenders.ivy-mix.career: Vermont. NYC. Worked at Clover Club with Julie Reiner. Co-founded Leyenda with Reiner. Co-created Speed Rack — competition for female bartenders raising funds against breast cancer ($1M+ raised).
wiki.art.bartenders.ivy-mix.signature: Latin spirits-based cocktails. Mezcal Pegu. Strawberries Forever. Style: agave-focused, Latin American spirits, female-driven bartending.
wiki.art.bartenders.ivy-mix.tips: Leyenda in Brooklyn — focus on agave, pisco, rum. Spirits of Latin America (2020) is excellent for understanding regional spirit diversity.
wiki.art.bartenders.ivy-mix.sources: Mix, Spirits of Latin America (2020). Leyenda archive. Speed Rack.
wiki.art.bartenders.lynnette-marrero.des: Lynnette Marrero (b. 1979), Puerto Rican-American bartender, co-founder of Speed Rack with Ivy Mix (2011). Advocate of female bartending and Latina presence in industry. Beverage director of several NYC bars.
wiki.art.bartenders.lynnette-marrero.car: NYC. Worked at Flatiron Lounge with Julie Reiner. Co-founded Speed Rack 2011. Beverage director Bar Centro (Joe Bastianich), Donna (Brooklyn). Educator and consultant.
wiki.art.bartenders.lynnette-marrero.sig: Latin-inspired cocktails. Tonight at the Bossa Nova. Style: bridge between Latina heritage and craft bartending. Pioneering Latina in American industry.
wiki.art.bartenders.lynnette-marrero.tip: Speed Rack is annual competition — watch finals in NYC, LA, etc. Marrero is the reference for Latina representation in professional bartending.
wiki.art.bartenders.lynnette-marrero.sou: Speed Rack archive. PUNCH — Latina bartenders. Eater NYC profiles.
wiki.art.bartenders.eryn-reece.title: Eryn Reece
wiki.art.bartenders.eryn-reece.descripti: Eryn Reece, American bartender, head bartender at Death & Co (NYC) during revival years. Co-author 'Death & Co: Welcome Home' (2021). Specialist in modern classics and new signatures.
wiki.art.bartenders.eryn-reece.career: NYC. Death & Co since around 2009. Became head bartender. Death & Co expanded to Denver, LA. Cross-bar team manager.
wiki.art.bartenders.eryn-reece.signature: Death & Co signatures: Conference Room. Eastside (Saunders style). Style: refined modern classics, craft moderate.
wiki.art.bartenders.eryn-reece.tips: Death & Co in East Village is must-visit. Welcome Home (2021) has 500+ home recipes.
wiki.art.bartenders.eryn-reece.sources: Death & Co: Welcome Home (2021). Death & Co archive. PUNCH.
wiki.art.bartenders.charles-schumann.des: Charles Schumann (b. 1941), German bartender from Munich, owner of Schumann's Bar (Munich, 1982 — since 2003 on Maximilianstrasse). Author of 'American Bar' (1991) and 'Tropical Bar' (1995). Patriarch of German-European bartending.
wiki.art.bartenders.charles-schumann.car: Munich since the 70s. Schumann's Bar 1982 — Germany's first serious cocktail bar. Influenced the entire later Germanic generation. Hugo Boss campaign model (70s-80s, known for his elegance).
wiki.art.bartenders.charles-schumann.sig: Schumann's signature menus. Style: elegant Bavarian bartender, classical conservatism, German precision.
wiki.art.bartenders.charles-schumann.tip: Schumann's on Maximilianstrasse (Munich) is must-visit if in Bavaria. 'American Bar' (1991) is a fundamental German/English text on classic cocktails.
wiki.art.bartenders.charles-schumann.sou: Schumann, American Bar (1991). Schumann, Tropical Bar (1995). Schumann's archive.
wiki.art.bartenders.kapri-robinson.title: Kapri Robinson
wiki.art.bartenders.kapri-robinson.descr: Kapri Robinson, American bartender, leading voice of Black bartending. Director of Hospitality at Allegory (DC). Co-founder of Chocolate City's Bartending Education for Black community. Speed Rack alumna.
wiki.art.bartenders.kapri-robinson.caree: Washington DC. Allegory (Eaton Hotel). Speed Rack alumna. Industry activism for racial diversification. Bartending education speaker.
wiki.art.bartenders.kapri-robinson.signa: Allegory signature cocktails. Storytelling-driven menus. Style: narrative cocktails about Black history.
